continuous_motion_budget_per_camera: 5 seconds of motion, regained at one second per 4s, charged in full before each continuous move starts
how_to_enable: control is already enabled on this server; cameras that have not opted in (cam-fixed) need an operator to set "control": true on their config entry and restart the server
explanation: when control is disabled, the write tools listed in gated_write_tools are not registered and do not appear in tools/list; when enabled the write tools still default to dry_run true (the halt tools do not, see below), so a caller must pass dry_run false to change a camera, and only cameras with control_allowed true accept it. control_allowed is a camera's own opt-in and only takes effect when control_enabled is true; writable says whether a camera can be controlled now. ptz.stop stops motion and is listed in gated_write_tools too, but has no dry run and is not rate limited: it is available whenever control is enabled and the camera opted in, so a stop is never held back by the movement rate limit. ptz.move_continuous moves for a requested duration and then stops the camera itself; it is registered only when at least one camera sets ptz_honours_timeout and refuses any camera that does not. That setting is the operator's claim, not something this server can check, that the camera ends the move by itself when the ONVIF Timeout sent with it runs out: if this server is killed, runs out of memory or loses power mid-move, that Timeout is the only remaining protection. It also draws on continuous_motion_budget_per_camera and holds the camera busy until it has stopped it
why: write tools physically move or reconfigure a real camera; an agent that loops on them can wear out or wedge the mechanism, so the operator has enabled control on this server and each camera must also opt in individually
